executive_summary: Rig Relay is a Python backend with a web frontend, currently hosted on macOS via pywebview (Cocoa/WebKit WKWebView). The desktop architecture is a single DesktopBridgeServer on one port serving both static assets and a token-gated WebSocket projection stream. The frontend is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with a runtime state machine, widget system, and reactive projection loop. The backend owns all state, policy, governance, agent orchestration, tool registry, analytics authority, and evidence authority. This audit verifies the published GitHub baseline at commit 6ac6d40b, inventories all desktop/frontend/data/script surfaces, defines the SwiftUI shell authority matrix, evaluates Safari Web Extension feasibility, maps the operational data plane from canonical JSON artifacts through DuckDB analytics to future PostgreSQL projections, evaluates Arrow/Vega-Lite for frontend data transport and visualization, defines the ML privacy boundary, reclassifies 22 promotion-candidate scripts into service/tool/projection/data-plane roles, and proposes a non-overlapping P1–P5 implementation ownership plan.

section_2_target_macos_host_architecture.title: Section 2 — Target macOS Host Architecture (SwiftUI Thin Shell)
section_2_target_macos_host_architecture.recommendation: Thin SwiftUI shell hosting one WKWebView displaying the same web frontend, communicating through a narrow authenticated bridge to the Python backend.
rationale_against_current_pywebview: pywebview creates an independent WKWebView — no native menu bar integration, no native toolbar, no accessibility tree, no dock integration, no native open/save panel
pywebview's JS bridge (evaluate_js) is unauthenticated from the perspective of the frontend — any Python->JS call is inherently trusted, limiting attack surface hardening
pywebview's file dialog support is limited to one call per window
pywebview cannot participate in macOS sandbox entitlements or security-scoped bookmark acquisition
pywebview provider windows share Safari's cookie jar — convenient for development but a privacy concern for production
pywebview's window lifecyle is managed by its own Cocoa runloop, not by SwiftUI's NSApplication lifecycle

must_own: App and window lifecycle (NSApplicationDelegate hooks, scene phases)
Menu bar intents (standard Edit/Copy/Paste, custom Rig Relay commands → backend intent)
Native open/save/folder pickers (NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel → backend path intake)
Drag and drop intake (NSItemProvider/UTType → backend registration)
Security-scoped bookmark acquisition (sandboxed distribution → backend path authorization)
Dock/menu-bar icon presentation with badge counts from backend projection
App activation and URL opening (custom URL scheme rig-relay:// → backend intent routing)
Appearance/accessibility forwarding (light/dark mode → CSS variable via WKWebView evaluateJavaScript)
WKWebView cookie and website data isolation (app-local, not shared Safari cookie jar)
WKUserScript injection for backend-derived runtime config (token, ws_url, origin) before page load
Safari extension messaging relay (native app group shared container → extension → backend)
Future App Intents / Shortcuts (Siri/Shortcuts → narrow capability registry → backend intent)
must_not_own: Any governance, policy, or authorization decisions
GitHub logic, A2A task state, or tool registry
Analytics querying, DuckDB or PostgreSQL database connections
Any duplicate of backend projection state
Bash command execution or subprocess management

bridge_protocol_requirements.transport: HTTPS + WSS on loopback (127.0.0.1), same DesktopBridgeServer
bridge_protocol_requirements.auth: Token-gated, generated by backend, injected into WKWebView via WKUserScript at load time
shell_to_backend_events: native_safari_extension_message: {event_type: str, payload_sha256: str, content_light: true}
backend_to_shell_events: shell_request_notification: {title: str, body: str, identifier: str}
bridge_protocol_requirements.principle: Shell sends bounded events; backend makes decisions; shell displays results. No state duplication.

section_2_target_macos_host_architecture.pywebview_retention: Retain pywebview as current development host and fallback for non-macOS platforms. SwiftUI is macOS-specific. pywebview is the primary host until SwiftUI shell ships.

section_3_safari_web_extension.title: Section 3 — Safari Web Extension Evaluation
section_3_safari_web_extension.recommendation: Defer to P4 (Native macOS Host wave) or later. Not in P1–P3.
section_3_safari_web_extension.rationale: The SwiftUI shell/backend bridge must prove stable before introducing cross-process browser extension messaging. The Safari extension is a companion capability, not a prerequisite for any P1–P3 service.
feasible_capabilities: Send selected text or page metadata from Safari to Rig Relay via native app group shared container
Forward GitHub issue/PR URLs for backend inspection and context packet enrichment
Forward documentation or error-page context into a governed context packet
Open Rig Relay to a projected view from toolbar button click
Display bounded backend status (active session count, last checkpoint) in extension popover

privacy_and_authority_contract.explicit_user_gesture_required: All content capture must require explicit user gesture (toolbar button click, context menu item)
privacy_and_authority_contract.no_silent_scraping: Must not silently scrape browsing activity into telemetry
privacy_and_authority_contract.no_github_credentials_in_extension: Must not hold GitHub credentials, tokens, or API keys
privacy_and_authority_contract.no_tool_execution: Must not execute tools, create checkpoints, or perform A2A mutations
privacy_and_authority_contract.no_policy_bypass: Must not bypass disclosure authorization or governance policy
privacy_and_authority_contract.content_light: Extension messages to backend are hashed (sha256) — raw page content never leaves browser context without explicit capture gesture and content-light envelope
privacy_and_authority_contract.minimum_viable_privacy: Safari extension does not connect to the internet itself — it communicates only with the Rig Relay native app through the native messaging/app group bridge

section_3_safari_web_extension.milestone: P4 or later. The prerequisite is a working SwiftUI shell that can receive app group messages.

section_5_operational_projection_port.title: Section 5 — Canonical Operational Projection Port
section_5_operational_projection_port.description: The P3 operational projection port is the normalized interface between canonical portable evidence (JSON/JSONL/CSV) and PostgreSQL operational tables. It preserves canonical artifact identity and never converts Postgres into source-of-truth. Postgres rows are rebuildable from canonical artifacts.

port_contract.principle: Every Postgres row is a content-light projection of a canonical artifact. The artifact is always the authority. Postgres rows can be dropped and rebuilt from artifacts.
required_fields_per_record: source_schema_version (string) — schema version of the source canonical artifact
source_artifact_digest (sha256 string) — SHA256 of the canonical source artifact
record_identity (string) — stable identity within the projection table (derived from source, not auto-increment)
event_or_receipt_identity (string|null) — if applicable, the canonical event/receipt identity
producer (string) — which subsystem produced this record (agent_loop, coordination, governance, github, a2a, telemetry)
timestamp_or_sequence (ISO8601 string) — when the source event occurred
outcome_classification (string) — simplified outcome (completed, failed, blocked, refused, pending)
authorization_requirement (string|null) — required authorization posture if applicable
projection_version (string) — version of this projection record format
idempotency_key (string) — deterministic replay key (hash of source_artifact_digest + record_identity)
payload_envelope (jsonb) — versioned bounded JSON content-light envelope
rebuildability_status (string) — 'rebuildable' (can regenerate from canonical artifact) or 'source_only' (canonical artifact is the sole authority, no separate record)

projection_table_recommendations.rejection_reason: A single universal event/projection ledger creates schema drift (every event type has different required fields), makes query performance dependent on jsonb indexes only, and mixes confidentiality tiers without column-level control. Typed projection tables per domain allow relational indexing on stable dimensions while using jsonb for versioned content.

section_6_postgresql_implementation_phas.title: Section 6 — PostgreSQL Implementation Phases
section_6_postgresql_implementation_phas.recommendation: Phase 1: Define the projection port + backend interface (P3). Phase 2: Add Psycopg 3 and first table implementation (P3 same slice or follow-up).

psycopg_evaluation.package_location: rig_relay/data/operational/ (new package, not adding to core or desktop)
psycopg_evaluation.dependency_declaration: uv add psycopg[binary] — declared as optional extras group 'postgres' or as a core dependency if P3 is non-optional
psycopg_evaluation.first_use: COPY for bulk ingest of canonical JSONL artifacts (receipts, coordination events) into typed projection tables
psycopg_evaluation.async_support: Psycopg 3 async connection pool — well-suited for async agent loop and projection refresh background tasks
psycopg_evaluation.test_environment: Tests require a running PostgreSQL instance. Options: (a) pg_tmp ephemeral database with pg_isready check, (b) Docker with testcontainers pattern, (c) GitHub Actions service container for CI. Recommend pg_tmp for local dev + CI service container for GitHub Actions.
psycopg_evaluation.no_sqlalchemy: Do NOT recommend SQLAlchemy or Alembic. Psycopg 3 direct SQL execution with typed projection builders is sufficient. No migration framework needed — projection tables are rebuildable from canonical artifacts.

copy_evaluation.fit: Bulk ingest for canonical JSONL → typed projection tables
copy_evaluation.usage: COPY governance_decisions FROM STDIN or COPY coordination_events FROM STDIN — rows are normalized during build, not during COPY
copy_evaluation.export: COPY ... TO STDOUT for bulk export of projection tables → rebuildable artifact verification
copy_evaluation.alternative: DuckDB reads JSONL, transforms, writes Parquet → Psycopg COPY reads Parquet → Postgres. Adds DuckDB buffer. Not needed for first slice — direct JSONL→Postgres row builder is sufficient.

listen_notify_evaluation.fit: Bounded cockpit invalidation signal — NOT state transport
listen_notify_evaluation.usage: Backend writes projection row → NOTIFY 'cockpit:governance_decisions' → WKWebView/WS receives event → frontend requests refresh of specific widget
listen_notify_evaluation.principle: Notification carries table name + optional filter key — never carries row data. Frontend issues get_projection request after invalidation.
listen_notify_evaluation.do_not_use_for: Real-time state streaming, event sourcing, transactional outbox, or replication

materialized_views.fit: Heavier dashboard summaries that join across tables
candidates: session_throughput_summary (per day/week, grouped by agent_profile, provider, model)
governance_decision_daily_summary (per day, by decision_kind and severity)
materialized_views.refresh_policy: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY on schedule or on demand — not on every write

roles_and_rls.usage: Roles: cockpit_reader (read-only), evidence_writer (insert projection rows), operator_admin (manage users). RLS: row-level security by team/tenant scope when multi-tenant operation is implemented.
roles_and_rls.timeline: P5 or later — requires tenant registry and hosted authentication infrastructure.

section_7_duckdb_parquet_role.title: Section 7 — DuckDB and Derived Snapshot Role
section_7_duckdb_parquet_role.recommendation: DuckDB remains a disposable read-side analytical projection over canonical artifacts. Parquet is a derived historical/analytical snapshot format, never a mutation authority.

existing_duckdb_projections.note: These views currently query from in-memory DuckDB tables built by AnalyticsEngine, not from a persistence layer

duckdb_vs_postgres_equivalence.requirement: Given the same canonical evidence corpus, a DuckDB analytical projection and Postgres operational projection should agree on bounded semantic records where they intentionally overlap.
duckdb_vs_postgres_equivalence.validation_mechanism: A cross-projection validation check (P3 scope): for each projected table with an equivalent DuckDB view, compare row counts, aggregate sums, and sampled hash matches. Emit validation report as canonical evidence.
duckdb_vs_postgres_equivalence.discrepancy_tolerance: Count-only differences may arise from timing (DuckDB snapshot vs Postgres live). Hash-equivalent records must match exactly.

parquet_role.not_authority_for: Mutations, evidence records, checkpoint commits, governance decisions

vega_lite_declarative_viz.recommendation: Use Vega-Lite declarative JSON visualization grammar for desktop charts

fit_assessment.backend_owned_viz_specs: Backend owns query, aggregation, authorization, provenance, and safe chart-spec generation. Frontend renders approved specifications and emits bounded interaction intents.
fit_assessment.supported_views: Timelines, histograms, layered CI/tool outcomes, faceted agent/provider comparisons, regression/trend analysis (with Vega-Lite transforms), density/quantile views, selection-driven drill-down, multi-view dashboards
fit_assessment.bundle_size: Vega-Lite + Vega runtime ≈ 300-400KB gzipped. Acceptable for desktop app (not a web SaaS). Minimal impact on WKWebView (localhost, no network latency).
fit_assessment.current_stack_fit: Vega-Lite requires a runtime JS library. Current frontend is vanilla JS with no build system. Adding Vega-Lite requires either (a) bundled script tag from CDN (not appropriate for local-only desktop), (b) vendored library in frontend/, or (c) a minimal build step. Vendoring a single vegalite.min.js in frontend/desktop/js/vendor/ is the simplest path.
fit_assessment.accessibility: Vega-Lite charts are SVG-based, which WKWebView renders natively. Screen reader descriptions can be added via Vega-Lite's description field. Not as accessible as semantic HTML tables but adequate for developer tooling.
fit_assessment.security: Vega-Lite specs are JSON documents. Backend must validate specs against Vega-Lite JSON Schema before emission. No eval() or Function() in Vega-Lite rendering.

arrow_js_evaluation.postpone_reason: Current projection payloads are small (< 1MB JSON). Arrow IPC improves transport for multi-megabyte tabular datasets. No current projection exceeds that threshold. Re-evaluate when derived datasets (coordination, checkpoint, findings) grow beyond thousands of rows in a single projection payload.
arrow_js_evaluation.when_to_introduce: When any single projection payload regularly exceeds 2MB JSON or when exploratory analytics tables exceed 10,000 rows in a single query result sent to the frontend.
arrow_js_evaluation.fallback: JSON projection contracts remain necessary even if Arrow is introduced — dashboard status cards and small widget data will always use JSON.
arrow_js_evaluation.build_impact: Apache Arrow JavaScript (apache-arrow npm package) requires a build system (npm/webpack/vite) — the current vanilla JS frontend has no build system. Introducing Arrow triggers a frontend toolchain decision that is not needed for P1–P3.

section_9_ml_privacy_boundary.title: Section 9 — ML Analysis Privacy Boundary
safe_by_default_features: Outcome classes (completed, failed, blocked, refused, cancelled)
Refusal reasons (enum values, not full reason text)
Provider and model category (provider name, model ID — not API keys)
Cost and latency where available (cost_estimate, latency_ms)
CI result classes (passed, failed, cancelled, skipped)
Pseudonymous coordination patterns (session ID hashes, task ID hashes, path hashes)
Tool invocation metadata (tool_name, status, determinism_class, mutation_class)
requires_explicit_disclosure_or_consent: Raw prompts (never in ML datasets — disclosure violated)
Raw source code (never in ML datasets — IP boundary)
Private GitHub issue bodies (never — third-party data)
Raw workflow logs / CI output (never in ML datasets)
Source diffs (never — use semantic change snippets instead)
Raw semantic change snippets with identifiers preserved (use anonymized snippets only)

required_fields: feature_provenance (per feature: source corpus, transformation, aggregation method)
exclusions (list of excluded fields with reasons)
source_digests (per source: file path hash, sha256, row count, date range)
truncation (max rows, max features, outlier capping)
content_light_guarantee (boolean — always true for ML datasets)

ml_disclosure_governance.principle: Default ML-ready datasets MUST remain content-light and privacy-legible. No raw prompts, no raw source code, no secrets, no private identifiers.
ml_disclosure_governance.consent_gate: Contribution of ML datasets to shared benchmarks requires separate explicit consent (commercial_dataset_license scope in telemetry_consent — never default).
ml_disclosure_governance.enterprise_ml: Enterprise operational ML (predicting lane blockage, estimating session cost, detecting coordination drift) operates on operational projections — which are already content-light. No additional disclosure required.
